name: Islamism
summary: Islamism holds that Islam is a complete way of life whose divine law should govern the state and society, so that sovereignty belongs to God alone and rulers administer the shari'a rather than make law. Its main theorists (Banna, Mawdudi, Qutb, and Khomeini for the Shi'i case) reject secularism, nationalism built on race or territory, and both capitalism and communism, offering an Islamic social and economic order with zakat, a ban on usury and moral regulation of public life. Strands differ on means, from Mawdudi's elected Amir and Shura, to Qutb's call for jihad against man-made systems, to Khomeini's rule by the jurist.
scope: The mainstream Islamist current as the defining reference works describe it: Hasan al-Banna and the Muslim Brotherhood, Abul A'la Mawdudi (Mawdudi, Maududi) and Jamaat-e-Islami, Sayyid Qutb, and Khomeini's doctrine of guardianship of the jurist, which the reference work says Sunni scholars reject. Answers rest on the texts of Mawdudi, Qutb and Khomeini and on the Encyclopedia of Islam and the Muslim World entries. It excludes post-Islamist parties that dropped the shari'a, quietist Salafism, Salafi-jihadist groups as separate subjects, and Islam as personal faith alone.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Mawdudi says no social distinctions should exist to safeguard the privileges of any class, race or dynasty.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Mawdudi holds that marriage, publicly known and witnessed, is the correct relationship between man and woman and the basis of the family.

ban-interest.rationale: Khomeini says Islam has radically prohibited usury and banking on it, and Mawdudi lists transactions with guaranteed gain to one party among those Islamic law makes illegal.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Mawdudi endorses restrictions on erotic music and obscene pictures as protection for the moral order, which covers only some art.

civilians-legitimate-targets.rationale: Mawdudi says it is never permissible to oppress women, children, the old, the sick or the wounded, even at war with the state.

civilizational-union.rationale: Mawdudi says citizenship should be common to all Islamic states, but the reference work notes most Islamists work within existing state boundaries.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Khomeini condemns imperialism as a plan to subjugate and corrupt Muslim peoples.

class-collaboration.rationale: Qutb condemns the communist class system as one resting on hatred and envy between classes.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Qutb calls systems based on class struggle corrupt theories whose adherents are enemies of mankind.

clerical-rule.rationale: Khomeini vests rule in the leading jurist, but Mawdudi has an elected Amir advised by a Shura with jurists as a sub-committee, and the reference work says Sunni scholars reject guardianship.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Khomeini condemns imperialist powers for taking Muslim lands' oil and minerals.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Mawdudi says the Amir keeps office only while he has the people's confidence and must resign when he loses it.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Qutb holds Islam the only divine way of life and other societies ignorant (jahili), so no culture is equal to it.

decent-living-guarantee.rationale: Mawdudi lists feeding the hungry, clothing the naked and treating the sick among rights an Islamic constitution guarantees to everyone.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Mawdudi counts jihad among duties of every Muslim and Qutb describes the Muslim as defending the homeland where the shari'a rules, even unto martyrdom.

democracy-best.rationale: Mawdudi accepts elections but denies popular sovereignty, holding that people and government alike must obey God's law whatever the electorate wants.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Qutb rejects the communist society as one built on class hatred, with the proletariat in place of the Roman nobles.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Mawdudi and Qutb attribute sovereignty exclusively to God (hakimiyya), and Mawdudi makes the people God's caliphs under his law rather than the source of authority.

dominated-front.rationale: The reference work describes pan-Islamism as arising to unify Muslims against Western domination and foreign occupation.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Khomeini declares hereditary succession wrong and invalid, and Mawdudi denies any dynasty can be Khalifah.

elective-rulers.rationale: Mawdudi has all adults elect the Amir, while Khomeini's guardianship vests rule in the most qualified jurist, which the reference work says Sunni scholars reject.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Mawdudi says rulers and ruled are subject to the same law, and Muslims and non-Muslim citizens alike in civil and criminal law.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Mawdudi calls ideologies forcing artificial economic equality mistaken, and holds that only equality of opportunity is right.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Qutb praises the Islamic community as open to all races and Mawdudi bases the community on belief, not race, colour or territory.

harm-principle.rationale: Mawdudi's state restricts conduct such as drinking, gambling and extra-marital sex because God forbids it.

human-decline-since-golden-age.rationale: Qutb holds that the Qur'anic generation was unique and that later societies, Muslims included, fell back into ignorance, and the reference work records the same view of decline in Salafiyya thought.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Mawdudi and Qutb reject race, colour, language and country as bases of community in favour of shared belief.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: The defining reference works describe Islamists as advocating an Islamic order defined by applying the shari'a, and Mawdudi's Islamic state legislates only within the limits God's law sets.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Mawdudi says Islamic law categorically rejects the manufacture and sale of liquor and other intoxicants.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Mawdudi's Islamic law makes adultery and professional dancing illegal means of livelihood and treats extra-marital sex as a criminal offence.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Qutb rejects the materialistic interpretation of history, holding human values and morals stable and not changeable.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Khomeini declares monarchy and hereditary succession invalid and Mawdudi says no dynasty can hold the caliphate, though the reference work notes some Islamists favour an Islamic monarchy.

more-religion-public.rationale: Mawdudi holds that Islam shapes individual and collective life alike, with no line between the spiritual and the secular.

national-rebirth.rationale: The Brotherhood aimed at a complete spiritual revival of society under Islam after a period of weakness.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Qutb treats communist and capitalist systems alike as results of rebellion against God's authority, and Mawdudi rejects both nationalised means of production and unbridled economic freedom for a middle course under divine law.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Mawdudi gives the state the purpose of promoting virtue and suppressing evil, well beyond protecting people from violence.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Mawdudi makes zakat on accumulated wealth a duty and says the rich must treat employees justly, enforced by the state.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Mawdudi gives the state the task of eradicating evils, and Qutb describes the struggle to establish God's rule against ignorance.

premarital-sex.rationale: Mawdudi holds all extra-marital sex sinful and forbidden and a criminal offence with severe punishments.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Mawdudi has the ruler govern under the shari'a, applied by an independent judiciary answerable to the law.

property-fundamental.rationale: Mawdudi accepts the right of ownership of legitimately earned wealth but says it is not unrestrained and the Islamic state may prohibit uses of it.

public-ownership.rationale: Mawdudi says nationalising the means of production leads to the annihilation of the individual by the community.

race-based-immigration-restrictions.rationale: Mawdudi grants citizenship to any Muslim who settles in an Islamic state regardless of birthplace and bars distinctions of race or colour.

racial-franchise.rationale: Mawdudi has all adult men and women who accept the constitution vote, and makes every Muslim eligible for the highest office without distinction of race, colour or class.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Qutb treats grouping by race and colour as a residue of the pre-Islamic ignorance that belief overcame.

racial-pride.rationale: Qutb calls pride of race, lineage and nationality a residue of ignorance that belief removes.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Mawdudi makes surrender to God and obedience to His commands the first obligation, ahead of independent human judgement.

religion-illusion.rationale: Mawdudi and Qutb present Islam as the true account of reality and a complete divine way of life, not a comfort.

religious-nation.rationale: Qutb says a Muslim's nationality is belief and his homeland the land where the shari'a rules, and Mawdudi describes the Muslim community as founded on belief rather than race, colour or territory.

religious-offensive-war.rationale: Qutb says Islam does not force belief but must fight the powers that bar people from accepting God's sovereignty until they submit or are defeated.

remove-other-ethnic-groups-from-country.rationale: Mawdudi holds that non-Muslim citizens' life, property and rights are irrevocable and protected equally with Muslims'.

restrict-private-adult-pornography-acces.rationale: Mawdudi lists restrictions on erotic music and obscene pictures and discouraging all forms of pornography among the measures that protect the family in an Islamic order.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Mawdudi names marriage between man and woman as the correct relationship, and Qutb counts homosexuality among immoral relations.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: Mawdudi and Qutb call the Qur'an the final Book of God and its law to be accepted without question.

separate-church-state.rationale: Mawdudi says Islam makes no distinction between the spiritual and the secular, and Khomeini calls the claim that religion should stay out of politics an imperialist invention.

separated-powers.rationale: Mawdudi describes an Amir, an elected Shura, and a judiciary independent of the executive, with legislation bounded by the shari'a.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Mawdudi gives the husband a position of authority as head of the household and expects the wife to obey him.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Qutb calls for abolishing man-made systems and replacing them with God's rule through the shari'a.

socialized-care.rationale: Mawdudi assigns the family, under the husband's authority, the care of its members and warns against a loose family system.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Mawdudi says rulers and ruled are subject to the same law, and even the highest executive can be summoned before a court.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Mawdudi makes the state's aim the moral and spiritual flourishing of life under God's law, with no separation of spiritual and secular.

state-harmful.rationale: Khomeini argues that a ruler and government are necessary to carry out God's law, and Mawdudi sets out the Islamic state's duties.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Mawdudi's state exists to uphold belief in God and His law.

state-supports-good-ways-of-life.rationale: Mawdudi gives the Islamic state the purpose of promoting the virtues God wants and suppressing the evils He forbids, using all the means at its disposal.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Mawdudi says every citizen has the right to criticise the Amir and his government.

taxation-theft.rationale: Khomeini and Mawdudi treat zakat and other Islamic taxes as obligatory, which the Islamic state levies and enforces.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: The Brotherhood sanctions Western ideas and technology as tools for Islam and Qutb wants a faith that keeps the benefits of modern science and technology.

traditional-family.rationale: Mawdudi calls the marital family the correct relationship and says threats to it strike at the roots of society.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Mawdudi says the Islamic state will not interfere with the personal law of non-Muslims.

universal-morality.rationale: Mawdudi says Islam lays down universal fundamental rights and moral requirements for humanity as a whole, binding in all circumstances.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Qutb and Mawdudi declare un-Islamic any government not based solely on the shari'a and urge fighting for an Islamic order, though the reference work says they hesitated to call for violent measures.

missingStatements.text: Law should reflect distinct roles for men and women in public life.
missingStatements.rationale: Mawdudi held that a woman's main duty is the household, supported veiling and seclusion, and opposed women as head of state or legislator.

missingStatements.text: Lending money at interest should be prohibited by law.
missingStatements.rationale: Mawdudi opposed all interest (riba), however small, and proposed profit-and-loss equity finance instead.

notes: Themes searched: state and law, religion and politics, family and sexual morality, economy and property, community and race, means (jihad, elections), imperialism. The defining texts read are Mawdudi's Islamic Way of Life, Qutb's Milestones and Khomeini's Islamic Government, with three Encyclopedia of Islam and the Muslim World entries; Mawdudi's Islamic Law and Constitution and Banna's tracts were not found online. Strands differ on elections, violence and monarchy, so those answers are medium or low. Economic, technological, environmental and many world-affairs statements are null because these sources record no position. The earlier audit rested mostly on Wikipedia; every earlier answer was checked and those these sources do not settle were nulled.
